notes.text: The source supplies this text as 81 page records, one Arabic text and one English text per page, with no division into numbered reports, no isnad and matn split, and no transmitter data. Each page record is therefore one entry here, in source order, with its printed page number when the source gives one.

records.text_ar: الْجُزْءُ الثَّانِي مِنْ نُسْخَةِ الزُّبَيْرِ بْنِ عَدِيٍّ أَبِي عَدِيٍّ الْكُوفِيِّ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ. رِوَايَةُ أَبِي الْفَضْلِ عِيسَى بْنِ مُوسَى بْنِ الْمُتَوَكِّلِ ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُفَيْرٍ ، عَنِ الْحَجَّاجِ ، عَنْ بِشْرٍ ، عَنْهُ. رِوَايَةُ أَبِي الْفَتْحِ هِلالِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ الْحَفَّارِ ، عَنْ أَبِي الْفَضْلِ ابْنِ الْمُتَوَكِّلِ. رِوَايَةُ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زِينَةَ ، عَنْ هِلالٍ. رِوَايَةُ الشَّيْخِ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْمَقْرِئُ ، عَنِ ابْنِ زِينَةَ. رِوَايَةُ الشَّيْخِ الْإِمَامِ الْعَالِمِ الْعَلامَةِ تَاجِ الدِّينِ أَبِي الْيَمَنِ زَيْدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ الْكِنْدِيِّ، عَنْهُ. بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَلا حَوْلَ وَلا قُوَّةَ إِلا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
records.text_en: The Second Part of the Copy of al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī Abū ʿAdī al-Kūfī al-Hamdānī. Transmission of Abū l-Faḍl ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ibn ʿUfayr, from al-Ḥajjāj, from Bishr, from him. Transmission of Abū l-Fatḥ Hilāl ibn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥaffār, from Abū l-Faḍl Ibn al-Mutawakkil. Transmission of Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zīna, from Hilāl. Transmission of the shaykh Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad al-Muqriʾ, from Ibn Zīna. Transmission of the shaykh, imam, scholar, and great learned man Tāj al-Dīn Abū l-Yumn Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd al-Kindī, from him. In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. There is no might and no power except through God, the Most High, the Most Great.

records.text_ar: 1 - أَخْبَرَنَا الشَّيْخُ الْإِمَامُ الْعَالِمُ الأَوْحَدُ الصَّدْرُ الْكَبِيرُ تَاجُ الدِّينِ أَبُو الْيَمَنِ زَيْدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ الْكِنْدِيُّ ، أَبْقَاهُ اللَّهُ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا الشَّيْخُ أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْمُقْرِئُ ، أنبا أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زِينَةَ ، أَنَبا أَبُو الْفَتْحِ هِلالُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ الْحَفَّارُ ، قَالَ: قَرَأْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْفَضْلِ عِيسَى بْنِ مُوسَى بْنِ الْمُتَوَكِّلِ عَلَى اللَّهِ ، قَالَ: أنبا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُفَيْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلِ بْنِ أَبِي حَثْمَةَ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ ، ثنا أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ الْحَجَّاجُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ بْنِ قُتَيْبَةَ الأَصْبَهَانِيُّ ، ثنا بِشْرُ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ، ثنا الزُّبَيْرُ بْنُ عَدِيٍّ ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: ‌ ‌«مَنْ تَرَكَ الْجُمُعَةَ ثَلاثًا مِنْ غَيْرِ ضَرُورَةٍ كُتِبَ مُنَافِقًا فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ لا يَمْحُو أَوْ لا يُبَدَّلُ»
records.text_en: 1 – The shaykh, imam, scholar, the unique one (al-awḥad), the great chief (al-ṣadr al-kabīr), Tāj al-Dīn Abū l-Yumn Zayd ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd al-Kindī — may God preserve him — informed us, saying: the shaykh Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad al-Muqriʾ informed us; Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zīna informed us; Abū l-Fatḥ Hilāl ibn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥaffār informed us, saying: I recited to Abū l-Faḍl ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā ibn al-Mutawakkil ʿalā Allāh, who said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUfayr ibn Muḥammad ibn Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathma al-Anṣārī informed us; Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf ibn Qutayba al-Aṣbahānī narrated to us; Bishr ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us; al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī narrated to us, from Anas ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever leaves the Friday prayer three times without necessity is recorded as a hypocrite in the Book of God, which neither erases nor is altered.”
translator_notes: The final clause لا يمحو أو لا يبدل is printed with active/passive forms that do not agree grammatically; translated closely as “which neither erases nor is altered”.

records.text_ar: 2 - وَبِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ: ‌ ‌«مَنْ تَرَكَ الْجُمُعَةَ تَهَاوُنًا بِهَا طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قَلْبِهِ»
records.text_en: 2 – And by his chain of transmission, he said: “Whoever leaves the Friday prayer out of negligence, God sets a seal upon his heart.”

records.text_ar: 3 - وَبِإِسْنَادِهِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: "‌ ‌ أَتَانِي جِبْرِيلُ بِمِرْآةٍ فِيهَا نُكْتَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ ، فَقُلْتُ: مَا هَذِهِ يَا جِبْرِيلُ؟ قَالَ: هَذِهِ الْجُمُعَةُ فُضِّلْتُ بِهَا أَنْتَ وَقَوْمُكَ ، وَاسْمُهَا عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ يَوْمُ الْمَزِيدِ ، قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ: فَمَا هَذِهِ النُّكْتَةُ؟ قَالَ: تَقُومُ فِيهَا السَّاعَةُ ، قُلْتُ: فَمَا يَوْمُ الْمَزِيدِ؟ قَالَ: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ تبارك وتعالى اتَّخَذَ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَادِيًا أَفْيَحَ فِيهِ كُثُبٌ مِنْ مِسْكٍ ، فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ نَزَلَ الرَّبُّ تبارك وتعالى ، وَحَفَّ مَجْلِسَهُ بِمَنَابِرَ مِنْ نُورٍ ، فَجَلَسَ عَلَيْهَا النَّبِيُّونَ ، وَحُفَّتْ تِلْكَ الْمَنَابِرُ بِمَنَابِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ مُكَّلَلَةٍ بِالْيَاقُوتِ وَالزَّبَرْجَدِ ، فَجَلَسَ عَلَيْهَا الصِّدِّيقُونَ وَالشُّهَدَاءُ ، وَنَزَلَ أَهْلُ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ ، فَكَانُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ ، فَيَقُولُ اللَّهُ: أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ قَدْ صَدَقْتُكُمْ وَعْدِى ، فَاسْأَلُونِي أُعْطِكُمْ. فَيَقُولُونَ: نَسْأَلُكَ رِضْوَانَكَ. فَيَقُولُ: قَدْ رَضِيتُ عَنْكُمْ وَلَدَيَّ مَزِيدٌ. وَلا يَوْمَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ "
records.text_en: 3 – And by his chain of transmission, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Jibrīl came to me with a mirror in which there was a black spot. I said: What is this, O Jibrīl? He said: This is Friday; you and your people have been favored with it, and its name with your Lord is the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazīd). He said: I said: And what is this spot? He said: The Hour will be established on it. I said: And what is the Day of Increase? He said: Your Lord, Blessed and Exalted, has made in Paradise a spacious valley in which are hills of musk; and when it is the day of Friday, the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends, and surrounds His assembly with pulpits of light, and the prophets sit upon them; and those pulpits are surrounded by pulpits of gold, crowned with rubies and chrysolite, and the truthful (ṣiddīqūn) and the martyrs sit upon them; and the people of the Gardens of Eden descend. They remain so, and God says: I am your Lord; I have been true to My promise to you; so ask Me and I shall give you. They say: We ask You for Your good pleasure (riḍwān). He says: I am pleased with you, and with Me there is more. And there is no day more beloved to them than the day of Friday.”

records.text_ar: 4 - وَبِهِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: «إِنَّ‌ ‌ أَغْبَطَ النَّاسِ عِنْدِي لَرَجُلٌ ذُو حَظٍّ مِنْ صَلاةٍ غَامِضٌ فِي النَّاسِ ، لا يُشَارُ إِلَيْهِ بِالأَصَابِعِ، وَيَمُوتُ إِذَا مَاتَ قَلِيلَ الْمِيرَاثِ وَالْبَوَاكِي، فَذَلِكَ صِفَةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ»
records.text_en: 4 – And by it, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The most enviable of people in my view is a man who has a share of prayer, obscure among people, not pointed out with fingers, who, when he dies, dies leaving little inheritance and few mourners; that is the description of the believer.”

records.text_ar: 5 - وَبِهِ قَالَ: أُهْدِيَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم طَيْرٌ مَشْوِيٌّ ، فَلَمَّا وُضِعَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ قَالَ: ‌ ‌«اللَّهُمَّ ائْتِنِي بِأَحَبِّ خَلْقِكَ إِلَيْكَ يَأْكُلُ مَعِيَ مِنَ الطَّيْرِ» . قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهُ رَجُلا مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ ، قَالَ: فَجَاءَ عَلِيٌّ عليه السلام ، فَقَرَعَ الْبَابَ قَرْعًا خَفِيًّا ، فَقُلْتُ: مَنْ هَذَا؟ قَالَ: عَلِيٌّ. فَقُلْتُ: إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى حَاجَةٍ ، فَانْصَرَفَ ، قَالَ: فَرَجَعْتُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وَهُوَ يَقُولُ الثَّانِيَةَ: «اللَّهُمَّ ائْتِنِي بِأَحَبِّ خَلْقِكَ إِلَيْكَ يَأْكُلُ مَعِيَ مِنْ هَذَا الطَّيْرِ» . فَقُلْتُ: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهُ رَجُلا مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ ، قَالَ: فَجَاءَ عَلِيٌّ ، فَقَرَعَ الْبَابَ ، فَقُلْتُ: أَلَمْ أُخْبِرْكَ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى حَاجَةٍ ، انْصَرَفَ ، فَرَجَعْتُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وَهُوَ يَقُولُ الثَّالِثَةُ: «اللَّهُمَّ ائْتِنِي بِأَحَبِّ خَلْقِكَ إِلَيْكَ يَأْكُلُ مَعِيَ مِنْ هَذَا الطَّيْرِ» . قَالَ: فَجَاءَ عَلِيٌّ فَضَرَبَ الْبَابَ ضَرْبًا شَدِيدًا ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «افْتَحْ افْتَحْ افْتَحْ» . قَالَ: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: «اللَّهُمَّ وَالِ ، اللَّهُمُّ وَالِ ، اللَّهُمَّ وَالِ» . فَجَلَسَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَأْكُلُ مَعَهُ الطَّيْرَ
records.text_en: 5 – And by it he said: A roasted bird was given as a gift to the Messenger of God ﷺ. When it was placed before him he said: “O God, bring me the one most beloved of Your creation to You to eat with me of the bird.” He said: I said to myself: O God, make him a man of the Anṣār. He said: Then ʿAlī ﵇ came and knocked at the door softly. I said: Who is this? He said: ʿAlī. I said: The Messenger of God ﷺ is occupied with something; so he left. He said: I returned to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he was saying for the second time: “O God, bring me the one most beloved of Your creation to You to eat with me of this bird.” I said: O God, make him a man of the Anṣār. He said: Then ʿAlī came and knocked at the door. I said: Did I not tell you that the Messenger of God ﷺ is occupied? Leave. I returned to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he was saying for the third time: “O God, bring me the one most beloved of Your creation to You to eat with me of this bird.” He said: Then ʿAlī came and struck the door violently, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Open, open, open!” He said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ looked at him, he said: “O God, befriend [him]; O God, befriend [him]; O God, befriend [him].” So he sat with the Messenger of God ﷺ, eating the bird with him.
translator_notes: In اللهم وال (“O God, befriend [him]”) the object is not expressed in the Arabic; “[him]” is supplied for sense.

records.text_ar: 6 - وَبِهِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: ‌ ‌«تَسَحَّرُوا؛ فَإِنَّ فِي السَّحُورِ بَرَكَةً»
records.text_en: 6 – And by it, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Eat the predawn meal (suḥūr), for in the predawn meal there is blessing.”

records.text_ar: 7 - وَبِهِ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: ‌ ‌«مَنْ قَتَلَ عَبْدَهُ قَتَلْنَاهُ ، وَمَنْ جَدَعَ عَبْدَهُ جَدَعْنَاهُ»
records.text_en: 7 – And by it he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever kills his slave, we shall kill him; and whoever mutilates his slave, we shall mutilate him.”

records.text_ar: 8 - وَبِهِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: ‌ ‌«مَنْ حَوَّلَ خَاتَمَهُ أَوْ عِمَامَتَهُ أَوْ عَلَّقَ خَيْطًا فِي إِصْبَعِهِ لِيُذَكِّرَهُ حَاجَتَهُ فَقَدْ أَشْرَكَ بِاللَّهِ ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ يُذَكِّرُ الْحَاجَاتِ»
records.text_en: 8 – And by it, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever shifts his ring or his turban, or ties a thread on his finger to remind him of his need, has associated partners with God; it is God alone who brings needs to mind.”

records.text_ar: 9 - وَبِهِ حَدَّثَنَا الزُّبَيْرُ ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، كَانَ‌ ‌ إِذَا رَأَى فِي أَهْلِهِ مُنْكَرًا ، قَالَ: «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ» . وَإِذَا رَأَى مَا يُحِبُّ ، قَالَ: «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الْمُنْعِمِ الْمُتَفَضِّلِ، اللَّهُمَّ بِنِعْمَتِكَ تَتِمُّ الصَّالِحَاتُ»
records.text_en: 9 – And by it al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Anas, that the Messenger of God ﷺ, when he saw something disliked among his family, would say: “Praise be to God in every circumstance.” And when he saw what he loved, he would say: “Praise be to God, the Bestower of favor, the Munificent; O God, by Your favor righteous deeds are completed.”

records.text_ar: 10 - حَدَّثَنِي الزُّبَيْرُ ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ‌ ‌ إِذَا قُدِّمَ إِلَيْهِ الطَّعَامُ ، قَالَ: «سُبْحَانَكَ وَبِحَمْدِكَ مَا أَكْثَرَ مَا تُعْطِينَا ، سُبْحَانَكَ وَبِحَمْدِكَ مَا أَعْظَمَ مَا تُعَافِينَا ، سُبْحَانَكَ وَبِحَمْدِكَ مَا أَحْسَنَ مَا تُبْلِينَا ، فَأَتْمِمْ عَلَيْنَا نِعْمَتَكَ ، وَوَسِّعْ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى فُقَرَاءِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ» . قَالَ: وَكَانَ إِذَا تَنَاوَلَ الطَّعَامَ يَقُولُ: «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ فِي أَوَّلِهِ وَآخِرِهِ» . وَكَانَ يَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ بَيْنَ كُلِّ لُقْمَتَيْنِ ، وَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَذْكُرُ اللَّهَ بَيْنَ كُلِّ خُطْوَتَيْنِ ، وَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا رَفَعَ يَدَهُ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ يَقُولُ: «أَطْعَمْتَ رَبِّي وَأَشْبَعْتَ ، لَكَ الْحَمْدُ فَهَنِّهِ ، أَكْثَرْتَ رَبِّي مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ ، لَكَ الْحَمْدُ فَزِدْ»
records.text_en: 10 – Al-Zubayr narrated to me, from Anas, that the Messenger of God ﷺ, when food was brought to him, would say: “Glory be to You and praise; how much You give us! Glory be to You and praise; how great is the well-being You grant us! Glory be to You and praise; how excellent is the trial with which You try us! So complete Your favor upon us, and make it ample for us and for the poor of the Muslims.” He said: And when he took the food he would say: “In the name of God, at its beginning and its end.” And he would praise God between every two morsels; and the Messenger of God ﷺ would remember God between every two steps; and the Messenger of God ﷺ, when he lifted his hand from the food, would say: “You have fed, my Lord, and satisfied; to You be praise, so let it be wholesome (fa-hanniʾhu); You have given abundantly of good things, my Lord; to You be praise, so increase.”

records.text_ar: 11 - وَبِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‌ ‌ إِذَا انْفَتَلَ مِنْ صَلاتِهِ مَسَحَ وَجْهَهُ بِيَدِهِ الْيُمْنَى ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لا إِلَهَ إِلا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ اللَّهُمَّ أَذْهِبْ عَنِّي الْهَمَّ وَالْحَزَنَ»
records.text_en: 11 – And by his chain of transmission he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ, when he turned away from his prayer, would wipe his face with his right hand, then say: “In the name of God, than whom there is no god, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate; O God, remove from me worry and grief.”

records.text_ar: 12 - وَبِهِ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: "‌ ‌ مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكْتَالَ لَهُ بِالْقَفِيزِ الأَوْفَى ، فَلْيَقُلْ: {فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ {17} وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ وَعَشِيًّا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ {18} يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَيُحْيِي الأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَكَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ {19} } [الروم: 17-19] . {سُبْحَانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ الْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ {180} وَسَلامٌ عَلَى الْمُرْسَلِينَ {181} وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ {182} } [الصافات: 180-182] "
records.text_en: 12 – And by it he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Whoever wishes to be measured out [his reward] with the fullest measure (qafīz), let him say: {So glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you rise in the morning {17} and to Him be praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the evening and when you are at midday {18} He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and gives life to the earth after its death; and thus you will be brought forth {19}} [al-Rūm: 17–19]. {Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe {180} and peace be upon the messengers {181} and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds {182}} [al-Ṣāffāt: 180–182].”

records.text_ar: 13 - وَبِهِ عَنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: ‌ ‌«قَرْضُ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي عَفَافٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ مَرَّةً»
records.text_en: 13 – And by it, from al-Zubayr, from Anas, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “A loan twice, in propriety (ʿafāf), is better than charity once.”

records.text_ar: 14 - وَبِهِ قَالَ: كَانَ أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ‌ ‌ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ اسْتَوَى قَائِمًا حَتَّى يُقِيمَ صُلْبَهُ ثُمَّ يَخِرُّ سَاجِدًا
records.text_en: 14 – And by it he said: Anas ibn Mālik, when he raised his head from bowing (rukūʿ), would stand upright until his spine was straight, then go down prostrating.

records.text_ar: 15 - وَبِهِ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَنَسٌ‌ ‌ عَنِ الصَّوْمِ فِي السَّفَرِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ أَمْ تَرْكُهُ؟ قَالَ: «أَنْ أَصُومَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ»
records.text_en: 15 – And by it he said: Anas was asked about fasting while travelling in the month of Ramaḍān: Is it more beloved to you, or leaving it? He said: “That I fast is more beloved to me.”

records.text_ar: 16 - وَبِهِ عَنْ أَنَسٍ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: ‌ ‌«غُسْلُ الْجُمُعَةِ وَاجِبٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ إِلا امْرَأَةً حَائِضًا أَوْ مَرِيضًا»
records.text_en: 16 – And by it, from Anas, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Friday bath (ghusl) is obligatory upon every Muslim, except a menstruating woman or a sick person.”

records.text_ar: 17 - وَبِهِ أَيْضًا، نا بِشْرٌ ، قَالَ: وَحَدَّثَ أَبُو سَعِيدٍ السِّجِسْتَانِيُّ ، عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ. يَعْنِي مِثْلَ حَدِيثِ أَنَسٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: ‌ ‌«غُسْلُ الْجُمُعَةِ وَاجِبٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُحْتَلِمٍ»
records.text_en: 17 – And by it also: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Abū Saʿīd al-Sijistānī narrated, from al-Qāsim, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of that — meaning the like of the report of Anas from the Prophet ﷺ — he said: “The Friday bath is obligatory upon every one who has reached puberty (muḥtalim).”

records.text_ar: 18 - وَبِهِ نا الزُّبَيْرُ ، قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ ، يَقُولُ: ‌ ‌«أَبَى اللَّهُ لِصَاحِبِ الْخُلُقِ الْمُسِيء بِالتَّوْبَةِ» . قِيلَ: وَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ يَا أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ؟ قَالَ: «لأَنَّهُ لا يَتُوبُ مِنْ ذَنْبٍ إِلا وَقَعَ فِي ذَنْبٍ أَعْظَمَ مِنَ الَّذِي قَدْ تَابَ مِنْهُ»
records.text_en: 18 – And by it al-Zubayr narrated to us, saying: Abū l-Dardāʾ used to say: “God has refused repentance to the one of bad character.” It was said: How is that, O Abū l-Dardāʾ? He said: “Because he does not repent of a sin except that he falls into a sin greater than the one he repented of.”

records.text_ar: 19 - نا الزُّبَيْرُ ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ ، قَالَ: "‌ ‌ يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ وَقَدْ خَرَجَ الْإِمَامُ إِذَا قَالَ الرَّجُلُ لِلنَّاسِ: أَنْصِتُوا ، فَقَدْ لَغَا عَلَى نَفْسِه "
records.text_en: 19 – Al-Zubayr narrated to us that Ibn Masʿūd said: “On the day of Friday, when the imam has come out: if a man says to the people ‘Be silent,’ he has engaged in idle talk against himself.”

records.text_ar: 20 - وَبِهِ نا الزُّبَيْرُ ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: ‌ ‌«لَيْسَ مِنَّا مَنْ ضَرَبَ الْخُدُودَ وَشَقَّ الْجُيُوبَ وَدَعَا بِدُعَاءِ أَهْلِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ» سَمِعْتُ الزُّبَيْرُ ، يَقُولُ: أَدْرَكْتُ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَيْسَ مِنْهُمْ رَجُلٌ يَبْتَاعُ لَحْمًا بِدِرْهَمٍ.
records.text_en: 20 – And by it al-Zubayr narrated to us that Ibn Masʿūd said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “He is not one of us who strikes the cheeks, tears the garments, and calls with the call of the people of the Jāhiliyya.” I heard al-Zubayr say: I met eighteen of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, none of whom would buy meat for a dirham.

records.text_ar: 21 - وَبِهِ حَدَّثَنِي الزُّبَيْرُ بْنُ عَدِيٍّ ، عَنْ طَارِقِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ ، قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ صَلاةَ الْغَدَاةِ فَلَمَّا‌ ‌ فَرَغَ مِنَ الْقِرَاءَةِ كَبَّرَ وَقَنَتَ بِهَاتَيْنِ السُّورَتَيْنِ فِي قِرَاءَةِ أُبَيٍّ ، ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَرَكَعَ
records.text_en: 21 – And by it al-Zubayr ibn ʿAdī narrated to me, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, who said: I prayed the morning prayer behind ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and when he had finished the recitation he said the takbīr and performed the qunūt with these two sūras, in the reading (qirāʾa) of Ubayy; then he said the takbīr and bowed.

records.text_ar: 22 - وَبِهِ عَنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، عَنِ الضَّحَّاكِ ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالإِحْسَانِ} [النحل: 90] . قَالَ: الْعَدْلُ صَلاةُ الْفَرِيضَةِ ، وَالإِحْسَانُ: قَوْلُهُ لا إِلَهَ إِلا اللَّهُ "
records.text_en: 22 – And by it, from al-Zubayr, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Indeed God commands justice and excellence (iḥsān)} [al-Naḥl: 90]. He said: Justice is the obligatory prayer, and excellence is saying: There is no god but God.

records.text_ar: 23 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، " فِي قَوْلِهِ: ‌ ‌{مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِنْهَا} [النمل: 89] . {وَمَنْ جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَكُبَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ} [ النمل: 90] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي بِالْحَسَنَةِ: التَّوْحِيدُ قَوْلُ: لا إِلَهَ إِلا اللَّهُ ، وَيَعْنِي بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا: يَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْهَا الْجَنَّةُ ، قَالَ: وَيَعْنِي بِالسَّيِّئَةِ الشِّرْكَ ، يَقُولُ: {فَكُبَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ} [النمل: 90] "
records.text_en: 23 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it} [al-Naml: 89]. {And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be cast into the Fire} [al-Naml: 90]. He said: By the good deed he means tawḥīd, the saying: There is no god but God; and by “better than it” he means: He says: for him from it is Paradise; he said: and by the evil deed he means polytheism (shirk); He says: {their faces will be cast into the Fire} [al-Naml: 90].

records.text_ar: 24 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ} [الأعراف: 156] . فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ الشِّرْكَ "
records.text_en: 24 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {And My mercy encompasses all things} [al-Aʿrāf: 156]. {So I shall decree it for those who guard against polytheism}.

records.text_ar: 25 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{يَسْلُكْهُ عَذَابًا صَعَدًا} [الجن: 17] . قَالَ: جَبَلٌ فِي النَّارِ زَلِقٌ كُلَّمَا صَعَدَ الْفَاجِرُ زَلِقَ فَيَهْوِي فِي النَّارِ "
records.text_en: 25 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {He will make him enter an arduous punishment (ʿadhāban ṣaʿadan)} [al-Jinn: 17]. He said: A slippery mountain in the Fire; whenever the wicked person climbs it he slips and falls into the Fire.

records.text_ar: 26 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ} [الفرقان: 27] . قَالَ: هُوَ عُقْبَةُ بْنُ أَبِي مُعَيْطٍ ، وَأُبَيُّ بْنُ خَلَفٍ "
records.text_en: 26 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {And on the Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands} [al-Furqān: 27]. He said: It is ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

records.text_ar: 27 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: " ‌ ‌{وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُونًا} [طه: 40] ابْتَلَيْنَاكَ ابْتِلاءً "
records.text_en: 27 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās: {And We tried you with trials (futūnan)} [Ṭāhā: 40]: We tested you with a test.

records.text_ar: 28 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ مَوْقُوفُونَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ} [سبأ: 31] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي الْمُشْرِكِينَ "
records.text_en: 28 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {If you could only see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord} [Sabaʾ: 31]. He said: He means the polytheists.

records.text_ar: 29 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{أَمْشَاجٍ نَبْتَلِيهِ} [الإنسان: 2] . يَعْنِي الْوَلَدَ مِنْ صُلْبِ أَبِيهِ وَصَرْفِ الأُمِّ ، خُلِقَ مِنْ سِتٍّ، ثَلاثٍ مِنْ قِبَلِ الأَبِّ: الْعَظْمُ وَالْعِرْقُ وَاللَّحْمُ ، وَثَلاثٍ مِنْ قِبَلِ الأُمِّ: الدَّمُ وَالشَّعَرُ وَالظُّفُرُ "
records.text_en: 29 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {mingled fluids (amshāj); We test him} [al-Insān: 2]. He means the child, from the loins of his father and the ṣarf of the mother; he is created from six: three from the father’s side: bone, sinew (ʿirq), and flesh; and three from the mother’s side: blood, hair, and nail.
translator_notes: “ṣarf of the mother” translates وصرف الأم as printed; the term is left untranslated because its sense here is unclear.

records.text_ar: 30 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{بَلَى قَادِرِينَ عَلَى أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ} [القيامة: 4] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي تُرَدُّ أَصَابِعُهُ فِي كَفِّهِ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ مِثْلَ حَافِرِ الْحِمَارِ "
records.text_en: 30 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Yes, [We are] able to restore his fingertips (banān)} [al-Qiyāma: 4]. He said: He means that his fingers will be turned back into his palm until it becomes like the hoof of a donkey.

records.text_ar: 31 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مِنَ الْمُسَحَّرِينَ} [الشعراء: 153] . قَالَ: مِنَ الْمَخْلُوقِينَ "
records.text_en: 31 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {You are only one of the bewitched (musaḥḥarīn)} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 153]. He said: Of the created ones.

records.text_ar: 32 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{أَزِفَتِ الآزِفَةُ} [النجم: 57] . قَامَتِ الْقِيَامَةُ "
records.text_en: 32 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {The imminent [Hour] has drawn near} [al-Najm: 57]. The Resurrection has arisen.

records.text_ar: 33 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{وَلا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلافٍ مَهِينٍ} [القلم: 10] . قَالَ: هُوَ أَبُو جَهْلٍ "
records.text_en: 33 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {And do not obey every vile oath-swearer} [al-Qalam: 10]. He said: It is Abū Jahl.

records.text_ar: 34 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ} [النحل: 38] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي أَبَا جَهْلٍ وَأُبَيَّ بْنَ خَلَفٍ "
records.text_en: 34 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {And they swore by God their strongest oaths} [al-Naḥl: 38]. He said: He means Abū Jahl and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

records.text_ar: 35 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{وَالسَّابِقُونَ الأَوَّلُونَ} [التوبة: 100] . قَالَ: أَبُو بَكْرٍ ، وَعُمَرُ ، وَعُثْمَانُ ، وَعَلِيٌّ ، وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ عَوْفٍ ، وَعَمَّارٌ ، وَسَلْمَانُ وَبِلالٌ ، وَصُهَيْبٌ "
records.text_en: 35 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {And the first forerunners} [al-Tawba: 100]. He said: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, ʿAmmār, Salmān, Bilāl, and Ṣuhayb.

records.text_ar: 36 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{ذَرْنِي وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيدًا} [المدثر: 11] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي الْوَلِيدَ بْنَ الْمُغِيرَةِ ، قَالَ: وَكَانَ لَهُ أَرْبَعَةُ آلافِ دِرْهَمٍ ، وَعَشْرُ بَنِينَ ، ذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: {وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالا مَمْدُودًا {12} وَبَنِينَ شُهُودًا {13} } [المدثر: 12-13] "
records.text_en: 36 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Leave Me with the one whom I created alone} [al-Muddaththir: 11]. He said: He means al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra; he said: He had four thousand dirhams and ten sons; that is His saying: {and I gave him extensive wealth {12} and sons present [with him] {13}} [al-Muddaththir: 12–13].

records.text_ar: 37 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، قَالَ: قِيلَ لَهُ: "‌ ‌ مَنْ أَحَبُّ النَّاسِ إِلَيْكَ؟ قَالَ: جَلِيسِي "
records.text_en: 37 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It was said to him: “Who is the most beloved of people to you? He said: My companion in sitting (jalīsī).”

records.text_ar: 38 - وَبِهِ قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فَقَالَ: إِنِّي‌ ‌ لا أَزَالُ أَسْأَلُ: أَمُؤْمِنٌ أَنْتَ؟ فَكَيْفَ أَقُولُ؟ قَالَ: " هَلْ أَذْنَبْتَ مُنْذُ آمَنْتَ؟ قَالَ: لا . قَالَ: فَأَنْتَ مُؤْمِنٌ ، ثُمَّ تَلا: {إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتَابُوا} [الحجرات: 15] "
records.text_en: 38 – And by it he said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: I keep asking: Are you a believer? — so how should I say? He said: “Have you sinned since you believed? He said: No. He said: Then you are a believer.” Then he recited: {The believers are only those who believe in God and His Messenger and then do not doubt} [al-Ḥujurāt: 15].
translator_notes: The verb is vocalized active (أَسْأَلُ, “I keep asking”); the sense may be passive (“I am constantly asked”). Translated as printed.

records.text_ar: 39 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَاؤُكُمْ غَوْرًا فَمَنْ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِمَاءٍ مَعِينٍ} [الملك: 30] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي مَاءَ زَمْزَمَ "
records.text_en: 39 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Say: Have you considered: if your water were to sink [into the earth], who would bring you flowing water?} [al-Mulk: 30]. He said: He means the water of Zamzam.

records.text_ar: 40 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ {219} فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةِ} [البقرة: 219-220] . قَالَ: يَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي الدُّنْيَا ، فَيَقُولُونَ: هِيَ دَارُ بَلاءٍ ، ثُمَّ هِيَ دَارُ شَقَاءٍ ، ثُمَّ هِيَ دَارُ زَوَالٍ ، وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي الآخِرَةِ ، فَيَقُولُونَ: هِيَ دَارُ جَزَاءٍ ، ثُمَّ هِيَ دَارُ نَعِيمٍ ، ثُمَّ هِيَ دَارُ بَقَاءٍ ، فَيَعْمَلُونَ لِلآخِرَةِ ، وَيَدَعُونَ الدُّنْيَا "
records.text_en: 40 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {so that you may reflect {219} on this world and the Hereafter} [al-Baqara: 219–220]. He said: They reflect on this world and say: It is an abode of trial, then it is an abode of misery, then it is an abode of passing away; and they reflect on the Hereafter and say: It is an abode of recompense, then it is an abode of bliss, then it is an abode of permanence; so they work for the Hereafter and leave this world.

records.text_ar: 41 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{يَأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ} [التحريم: 6] . قَالَ: يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ فِي أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ فَيَعْمَلُ تِلْكَ الأَعْمَالَ الصَّالِحَةَ ، يُصَلِّي فَيُصَلُّونَ ، وَيَصُومُ فَيَصُومُونَ ، وَيَتَصَدَّقُ فَيَتَصَدَّقُونَ ، فَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: {قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ} [التحريم: 6] "
records.text_en: 41 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones} [al-Taḥrīm: 6]. He said: The righteous servant is among a household and does those righteous deeds; he prays and they pray, he fasts and they fast, he gives charity and they give charity; that is His saying: {protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones} [al-Taḥrīm: 6].

records.text_ar: 42 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ وَاسْمَعُوا وَأَطِيعُوا وَأَنْفِقُوا خَيْرًا لأَنْفُسِكُمْ} [التغابن: 16] . يَعْنِي أَنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْتُكُمْ حَيْثُ أَمَرْتُكُمْ فِي الصِّلَةِ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ، يَعْنِي: {وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ} [التغابن: 16] . قَالَ: مَنْ أَدَّى زَكَاةَ مَالِهِ فَقَدْ وُقِيَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ "
records.text_en: 42 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {So fear God as much as you are able, and listen and obey, and spend; it is better for yourselves} [al-Taghābun: 16]. He means: spend from what I have provided you, where I commanded you: on kinship ties, the poor, the wayfarer, and in the way of God; he means: {and whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul} [al-Taghābun: 16]. He said: Whoever pays the zakāt on his wealth has been protected from the stinginess of his soul.

records.text_ar: 43 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{ثُمَّ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ} [التكاثر: 8] . قَالَ: الأَمْنُ وَصِحَّةُ الْجِسْمِ "
records.text_en: 43 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Then, on that Day, you will surely be asked about the bounty (naʿīm)} [al-Takāthur: 8]. He said: Security and bodily health.

records.text_ar: 44 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ} [الحج: 61] . قَالَ: هُوَ أَخَذَ اللَّيْلَ مِنَ النَّهَارِ ، وَأَخَذَ النَّهَارَ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ "
records.text_en: 44 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night} [al-Ḥajj: 61]. He said: He takes the night from the day, and takes the day from the night.

records.text_ar: 45 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ} [يونس: 31] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي النُّطْفَةَ ، يُخْرِجُهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَهِيَ مَيْتَةٌ ، ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُهُ اللَّهُ "
records.text_en: 45 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living} [Yūnus: 31]. He said: He means the sperm-drop (nuṭfa); God brings it forth from the living while it is dead, then God brings it forth
translator_notes: The report breaks off in the Arabic (ثم يخرجه الله) and is translated as it stands.

records.text_ar: 46 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، " ‌ ‌{أَيَّامٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ} [الحج: 28] . قَالَ: هِيَ أَيَّامُ الْعَشْرِ أَوَّلَ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ "
records.text_en: 46 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās: {known days (ayyām maʿlūmāt)} [al-Ḥajj: 28]. He said: They are the days of the ten, the beginning of Dhū l-Ḥijja.

records.text_ar: 47 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ} [البقرة: 184] . قَالَ: هُنَّ أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ "
records.text_en: 47 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {a limited number of days (ayyāman maʿdūdāt)} [al-Baqara: 184]. He said: They are the days of tashrīq.

records.text_ar: 48 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ} [البقرة: 196] . قَالَ: قَبْلَ التَّرْوِيَةِ بِيَوْمٍ ، وَيَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ ، وَيَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ "
records.text_en: 48 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {three days during the pilgrimage} [al-Baqara: 196]. He said: A day before the Day of Tarwiya, the Day of Tarwiya, and the Day of ʿArafa.

records.text_ar: 49 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{أَيَّامٍ نَحِسَاتٍ} [فصلت: 16] . قَالَ: آخِرُ شَوَّالٍ مِنَ الأَرْبَعَاءِ إِلَى الأَرْبَعَاءِ ، وَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: {سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا} [الحاقة: 7] "
records.text_en: 49 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {ill-omened days (ayyām naḥisāt)} [Fuṣṣilat: 16]. He said: The end of Shawwāl, from Wednesday to Wednesday; and that is His saying: {seven nights and eight days in succession} [al-Ḥāqqa: 7].

records.text_ar: 50 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِنَّ‌ ‌ الشَّيْطَانَ فَقِيهٌ غَيْرُ رَشِيدٍ»
records.text_en: 50 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: “Indeed, Satan is a jurist (faqīh), but not rightly guided.”

records.text_ar: 51 - عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{قُلْ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا} [يونس: 58] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ: الْقُرْآنُ ، وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا يَعْنِي: مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم. " ثُمَّ تَلا {وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلا رَحْمَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ} [الأنبياء: 107]
records.text_en: 51 – From Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Say: In the bounty of God and in His mercy — in that let them rejoice} [Yūnus: 58]. He said: He means by “the bounty of God”: the Qurʾān; and “in His mercy let them rejoice” means: Muḥammad ﷺ. Then he recited: {And We did not send you except as a mercy to the worlds} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 107].

records.text_ar: 52 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا} [الفرقان: 59] . يَعْنِي: سَلْ بِهِ جِبْرِيلَ عليه السلام "
records.text_en: 52 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {so ask about Him one who is well-informed} [al-Furqān: 59]. He means: ask Jibrīl ﵇ about Him.

records.text_ar: 53 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيَانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ} [الصف: 4] . مَنْ هَؤُلاءِ. قَالَ: حَمْزَةُ أَسَدُ اللَّهِ وَأَسَدُ رَسُولِهِ ، وَعَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ ، وَعُبَيْدَةُ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ ، وَالْمِقْدَادُ بْنُ الأَسْوَدِ "
records.text_en: 53 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Indeed God loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as though they were a solid structure} [al-Ṣaff: 4]. Who are these? He said: Ḥamza, the lion of God and the lion of His Messenger; ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib; ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith; and al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad.

records.text_ar: 54 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{سَفِيهُنَا عَلَى اللَّهِ شَطَطًا} [الجن: 4] . قَالَ: هُوَ إِبْلِيسُ "
records.text_en: 54 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {our foolish one used to say an outrageous falsehood about God} [al-Jinn: 4]. He said: It is Iblīs.

records.text_ar: 55 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{مَذْمُومًا مَدْحُورًا} [الإسراء: 18] . قَالَ: الْمَذْمُومُ: هُوَ الْمَلْعُونُ ، وَالْمَدْحُورُ: الْمَنْفِيُّ الْمَطْرُودُ "
records.text_en: 55 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {disgraced and driven away (madhmūman madḥūran)} [al-Isrāʾ: 18]. He said: The madhmūm is the accursed one, and the madḥūr is the banished, the expelled.

records.text_ar: 56 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: " ‌ ‌{زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ} [هود: 106] . قَالَ: الزَّفِيرُ أَنِينُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ ، وَالشَّهِيقُ النَّفَسُ الْعَالِي "
records.text_en: 56 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās: {sighing and wailing (zafīr wa-shahīq)} [Hūd: 106]. He said: The zafīr is the groaning of the people of the Fire, and the shahīq is the labored breath.

records.text_ar: 57 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ‌ ‌ عَنِ الأَحْقَافِ ، قَالَ: «جِبَالٌ فِي الشَّامِ مِنْ رِمَالٍ ، يُقَالُ لَهُ» . فَسَكَتَ
records.text_en: 57 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he was asked about al-Aḥqāf; he said: “Mountains of sand in Syria; it is said of it —” and he fell silent.
translator_notes: The report breaks off in the Arabic (يقال له ... فسكت): the name is not given.

records.text_ar: 58 - عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَغْفِرُوا لِلَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ اللَّهِ} [الجاثية: 14] . قَالَ: كَانَ بَيْنَ يَهُودِيٍّ وَبَيْنَ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ كَلامٌ فِي التَّوْحِيدِ ، فَأَغْلَظَ لَهُ عُمَرُ "
records.text_en: 58 – From Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not hope for the days of God} [al-Jāthiya: 14]. He said: There was an exchange between a Jew and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵀ about tawḥīd, and ʿUmar spoke harshly to him.

records.text_ar: 59 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَا الثَّقَلانِ} [الرحمن: 31] . قَالَ: الثَّقَلانِ: الْجِنُّ وَالإِنْسُ. وَقَوْلُهُ {سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ} [ الرحمن: 31] . وَعِيدٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ "
records.text_en: 59 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {We shall attend to you, O you two weighty ones (al-thaqalān)} [al-Raḥmān: 31]. He said: The two weighty ones are the jinn and humankind. And His saying {We shall attend to you} [al-Raḥmān: 31] is a threat from God.

records.text_ar: 60 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{وَبَشِّرِ الْمُخْبِتِينَ {34} الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَالصَّابِرِينَ عَلَى مَا أَصَابَهُمْ وَالْمُقِيمِي الصَّلاةِ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ {35} } [الحج: 34-35] . قَالَ: أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرُ وَعَلِيٌّ وَسَلْمَانُ "
records.text_en: 60 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {And give good tidings to the humble {34} those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and the patient over what afflicts them, and those who establish prayer, and who spend from what We have provided them {35}} [al-Ḥajj: 34–35]. He said: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿAlī, and Salmān.

records.text_ar: 61 - وَعَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فِي قَوْلِهِ: " ‌ ‌{وَلا تُطِعْ مَنْ أَغْفَلْنَا قَلْبَهُ عَنْ ذِكْرِنَا} [الكهف: 28] . قَالَ: يَعْنِي أَبَا جَهْلٍ "
records.text_en: 61 – And from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: {and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance} [al-Kahf: 28]. He said: He means Abū Jahl.

records.text_ar: 62 - وَبِهِ أنبا الْحَجَّاجُ ، ثنا النُّعْمَانُ بْنُ عَبْدِ السَّلامِ ، ثنا يَزِيدُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ التُّسْتَرِيُّ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ ، قِيلَ لَهُ: أَلا تُجَاهِدُ؟ فَسَكَتَ ، فَسَأَلَهُ ، فَسَكَتَ ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ: "‌ ‌ بُنِيَ الْإِسْلامُ عَلَى خَمْسٍ: عَلَى شَهَادَةِ أَنْ لا إِلَهَ إِلا اللَّهُ ، وَإِقَامِ الصَّلاةِ ، وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ ، وَحِجِّ الْبَيْتِ ، وَصَوْمِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ "
records.text_en: 62 – And by it al-Ḥajjāj informed us: al-Nuʿmān ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us: Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm al-Tustarī narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr: it was said to him: Will you not wage jihād? He fell silent; he asked him, and he fell silent. He said: Then Ibn ʿUmar said: “Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God, the establishment of prayer, the payment of zakāt, the pilgrimage to the House, and the fasting of the month of Ramaḍān.”
translator_notes: It is unclear from the Arabic who is silent and who is the asker in this exchange (قيل له ... فسكت، فسأله، فسكت); translated closely.

records.text_ar: 63 - وَبِهِ ثنا الْحَجَّاجُ ، ثنا النُّعْمَانُ بْنُ عَبْدِ السَّلامِ ، ثنا سُفْيَانُ الثَّوْرِيُّ ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ السَّبِيعِيِّ ، عَنْ أَبِي حَبِيبٍ الطَّائِيِّ ، قَالَ: مَاتَ أَخٌ لِي فَأَوْصَى إِلَيَّ ، وَأَوْصَى بِبَعْضِ مَالِهِ ، قَالَ: فَأَتَيْتُ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ ، أَسْأَلُهُ أَنْ أَجْعَلَ فِي الْمَسَاكِينِ وَالْفُقَرَاءِ ، قَالَ أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ: أَمَا لَوْ كُنْتُ أَنَا لَجَعَلْتُهُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ عز وجل ، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: ‌ ‌«مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَعْتِقُ عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يُهْدِي بَعْدَ مَا شَبِعَ» . وَالصَّوَابُ عَنْ أَبِي حَبِيبَةَ الطَّائِيِّ ، وَلَكِنْ كَذَا قَالَ الشَّيْخُ. يَعْنِي الْحَجَّاجَ
records.text_en: 63 – And by it al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us: al-Nuʿmān ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us: Sufyān al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī, from Abū Ḥabīb al-Ṭāʾī, who said: A brother of mine died and appointed me executor and bequeathed part of his property. He said: So I came to Abū l-Dardāʾ, asking him whether I should put it toward the poor and the needy. Abū l-Dardāʾ said: Were I in your place, I would put it in the way of God, Mighty and Majestic. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The likeness of one who frees [a slave] at the time of death is like that of one who gives a gift after he has eaten his fill.” And the correct [form] is from Abū Ḥabība al-Ṭāʾī, but thus the shaykh said — meaning al-Ḥajjāj.

records.text_ar: 64 - وَبِهِ ثنا الْحَجَّاجُ ، ثنا النُّعْمَانُ ، عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَطَاءٍ ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: ‌ ‌«سَلُوا اللَّهَ لِيَ الْوَسِيلَةَ ، لا يَسْأَلُهَا لِي مُؤْمِنٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا إِلا كُنْتُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا أَوْ شَهِيدًا» وَبِهِ ثنا النُّعْمَانُ ، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ الثَّوْرِيِّ ، عَنْ أَبِي الْهَيْثَمِ ، قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ النَّخَعِيَّ صَلَّى فِي مَرَضِهِ عَلَى جَنْبِهِ الأَيْمَنِ. وَبِهِ ثنا مِسْعَرُ بْنُ كِدَامٍ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ابْنِ الأَصْبَهَانِيُّ ، أَنَّهُ رَأَى أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ السُّلَمِيَّ يُسِرُّ رَجُلا يَدْعُو قَائِمًا بَعْدَ مَا انْفَتَلَ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ.
records.text_en: 64 – And by it al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us: al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Ask God for the wasīla for me; no believer asks it for me in this world but that I shall be an intercessor or a witness for him on the Day of Resurrection.” And by it al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Abū l-Haytham, who said: I saw Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī pray during his illness on his right side. And by it Misʿar ibn Kidām narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aṣbahānī, that he saw Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī speaking privately to a man, supplicating while standing, after he had turned away from the prayer.
translator_notes: The phrase يسر رجلا يدعو قائما is syntactically unclear in the Arabic and is translated closely.

records.text_ar: 65 - وَبِهِ ثنا النُّعْمَانُ ، ثنا شَرِيكُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ النَّخَعِيُّ ، عَنْ عُثْمَانَ الثَّقَفِيِّ ، عَنْ أَبِي لَيْلَى الْكِنْدِيِّ، عَنْ سُوَيْدِ بْنِ غَفْلَةَ ، قَالَ: أَتَانَا مُصَدِّقُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فَأَخَذْتُ بِيَدِهِ وَقَرَأْتُ فِي عَهْدِهِ: ‌ ‌«أَنْ لا تَجْمَعَ بَيْنَ مُتَفَرِّقٍ، وَلا تُفَرِّقَ بَيْنَ الْمُجْتَمِعِ» . وَأَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ بِنَاقَةٍ عَظِيمَةٍ مُلَمْلَمَةٍ ، فَأَبَى أَنْ يَأْخُذَهَا ، ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ بِدُونِهَا فَأَبَى أَنْ يَأْخُذَهَا ، ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ بِدُونِهَا فَأَبَى أَنْ يَأْخُذَهَا ، ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ بِدُونِهَا فَأَخَذَهَا ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَيُّ سَمَاءٍ تُظِلُّنِي ، وَأَيُّ أَرْضٍ تُقِلُّنِي ، إِنْ أَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَقَدْ أَخَذْتُ خِيَارَ إِبِلِ رَجُلٍ مُسْلِمٍ
records.text_en: 65 – And by it al-Nuʿmān narrated to us: Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nakhaʿī narrated to us, from ʿUthmān al-Thaqafī, from Abū Laylā al-Kindī, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, who said: The alms collector (muṣaddiq) of the Messenger of God ﷺ came to us; I took him by the hand and read in his covenant: “Do not combine what is separate, and do not separate what is combined.” A man came to him with a great, plump she-camel, and he refused to take it; then he brought him one lesser than it, and he refused to take it; then he brought him one lesser than it, and he refused to take it; then he brought him one lesser than it, and he took it. Then he said: What sky will shade me, and what earth will bear me, if I come to the Messenger of God ﷺ having taken the best of the camels of a Muslim man?

records.text_ar: 66 - حَدَّثَنَا الْحَجَّاجُ ، ثنا بِشْرٌ ، ثنا الزُّبَيْرُ ، قَالَ: قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: ‌ ‌«عَجِبْتُ لِلتَّاجِرِ كَيْفَ يَسْلَمُ إِذَا بَاعَ أَطْرَى وَإِذَا اشْتَرَى ذَمَّ ، مَا رَجُلٌ أَكْسَبُ مِنْ رَجُلٍ ، وَلا عَامٌ بِأَكْثَرَ مَطَرًا مِنْ عَامٍ ، وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ ، وَيَصْرِفُ الْمَطَرَ حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ»
records.text_en: 66 – Al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us: Bishr narrated to us: al-Zubayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Masʿūd said: “I am amazed at the merchant: how does he remain safe, when if he sells he extols [his goods] and if he buys he disparages? No man earns more than another man, and no year has more rain than another year; rather, God provides for whom He wills, and directs the rain where He wills.”

records.text_ar: 67 - وَبِهِ عَنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، عَنِ الْمَعْرُورِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ ، قَالَ: قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ: ‌ ‌«أَتَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ إِذَا نَهَاكَ ، وَإِذَا لَمْ يَنْهَكَ فَلَسْتَ تَقْرَؤُهُ»
records.text_en: 67 – And by it, from al-Zubayr, from al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “Do you recite the Qurʾān when it restrains you? And when it does not restrain you, you are not [truly] reciting it.”

records.text_ar: 68 - وَبِهِ عَنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، قَالَ: سُئِلَ حُذَيْفَةُ‌ ‌ عَنِ النِّفَاقِ ، فَقَالَ: «مَنْ تَوَضَّأَ فِي مَكَانٍ لا يَرَاهُ أَحَدٌ إِلا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَدْ بَرِئَ مِنَ النِّفَاقِ» . ثُمَّ قَالَ: " إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقَ مَنْ إِذَا خَلا لا يُصَلِّي ، وَكَذَلِكَ قَوْلُ اللَّهِ: {وَإِذَا خَلَوْا إِلَى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قَالُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ} [البقرة: 14] "
records.text_en: 68 – And by it, from al-Zubayr, who said: Ḥudhayfa was asked about hypocrisy (nifāq), and he said: “Whoever performs ablution in a place where no one sees him but God, then prays two rakʿas, has been cleared of hypocrisy.” Then he said: “The hypocrite is one who, when alone, does not pray; and likewise is the saying of God: {And when they are alone with their devils, they say: We are with you; we are only mocking} [al-Baqara: 14].”

records.text_ar: 69 - وَعَنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، قَالَ: قَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: ‌ ‌«إِنَّا أُوتِينَا الإِيمَانَ ، ثُمَّ أُوتِينَا الْقُرْآنَ ، وَسَيَجِيءُ بَعْدَكُمْ أَقْوَامٌ يُؤْتَوْنَ الْقُرْآنَ وَلا يُؤْتَوْنَ الإِيمَانَ»
records.text_en: 69 – And from al-Zubayr, who said: Ibn Masʿūd said: “We were given faith, then we were given the Qurʾān; and after you there will come peoples who are given the Qurʾān but are not given faith.”

records.text_ar: 70 - وَبِهِ ثنا الزُّبَيْرُ ، عَنِ الْمَعْرُورِ ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: ‌ ‌«الذَّهَبُ بِالذَّهَبِ ، وَالْفِضَّةُ بِالْفِضَّةِ ، وَالْبُرُّ بِالْبُرِّ ، وَالشَّعِيرُ بِالشَّعِيرِ ، وَالتَّمْرُ بِالتَّمْرِ ، وَالزَّبِيبُ بِالزَّبِيبِ ، وَالْمِلْحُ بِالْمِلْحِ ، مِثْلا بِمِثْلٍ، يَدًا بِيَدٍ ، فَمَنْ زَادَ أَوِ اسْتَزَادَ فَقَدْ أَرْبَى»
records.text_en: 70 – And by it al-Zubayr narrated to us, from al-Maʿrūr, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, raisins for raisins, salt for salt — like for like, hand to hand; whoever gives more or asks for more has practised usury (ribā).”

records.text_ar: 71 - وَبِهِ عَنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، عَنِ الْحَارِثِ الأَعْوَرِ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ ، قَالَ: قَالَ عَلِيٌّ عليه السلام: "‌ ‌ ثَلاثٌ بَعْدَهُنَّ ثَلاثٌ: وَأْدُ الْبَنَاتِ ، وَعُقُوقُ الْوَالِدَاتِ ، وَمَنْعُ وَهَاتِ . وَبَعْدَهُنَّ ثَلاثٌ: إِضَاعَةُ الْمَالِ ، وَإِلْحَافُ السُّؤَالِ ، وَقِيلَ وَقَالَ "
records.text_en: 71 – And by it, from al-Zubayr, from al-Ḥārith al-Aʿwar al-Hamdānī, who said: ʿAlī ﵇ said: “Three, after which come three: burying daughters alive, disobedience to mothers, and withholding and demanding (manʿ wa-hāt). And after them, three: squandering wealth, importunate begging, and idle talk (qīla wa-qāla).”

records.text_ar: 72 - وَبِهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ ، قَالَ: "‌ ‌ ثَلاثٌ مِنْ رَأْسِ التَّوَاضُعِ: أَنْ تَبْدَأَ بِالسَّلامِ مَنْ لَقِيتَ ، وَتَرْضَى بِالدُّونِ مِنْ شَرَفِ الْمَجْلِسِ ، وَتَكْرَهُ الرِّيَاءَ وَالسُّمْعَةَ بِالْبِرِّ "
records.text_en: 72 – And by it, from ʿAlī, who said: “Three things are at the head of humility: that you greet first whomever you meet, that you are content with a lower seat than the place of honor in the gathering, and that you dislike ostentation (riyāʾ) and showing off (sumʿa) in righteous deeds.”

records.text_ar: 73 - وَبِهِ قَالَ: خَرَجَ عَلِيٌّ عليه السلام ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى الرَّحْبَةِ ، وَقَالَ: " أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ‌ ‌ خَمْسٌ احْفَظُوهُنَّ عَنِّي ، فَلَوْ رَكِبْتُمُ الْمَطِيَّ لأَنْضَيْتُمُوهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ لا تَجِدُوا مَنْ يُخْبِرُكُمْ بِهِنَّ: أَلا لا يَخَافَنَّ الْعَبْدُ إِلا ذَنْبَهُ ، وَلا يَرْجُوَنَّ إِلا رَبَّهُ ، أَلا فَلا يَسْتَحِيَنَّ الْعَبْدُ إِذَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنْ يَتَعَلَّمَ ، وَلا يَسْتَحِيَنَّ إِذَا سُئِلَ عَمَّا لا يَعْلَمُ أَنْ يَقُولَ: اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ؛ فَإِنَّ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ أَنْ تَقُولَ لِمَا لا تَعْلَمُ: اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ ، أَلا وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الصَّبْرَ مِنَ الإِيمَانِ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الرَّأْسِ مِنَ الْجَسَدِ ، فَإِذَا قُطِعَ الرَّأْسُ ذَهَبَ الْجَسَدُ ، وَلا إِيمَانَ لِمَنْ لا صَبْرَ لَهُ "
records.text_en: 73 – And by it he said: ʿAlī ﵇ went out one night to the Raḥba and said: “O people, five [things]; preserve them from me, for if you were to ride riding-beasts you would wear them out before you found anyone to tell you of them: Let the servant fear nothing but his sin, and hope for nothing but his Lord. And let the servant not be shy, when he does not know, to learn; and let him not be shy, when asked about what he does not know, to say: God knows best; for part of knowledge is that you say of what you do not know: God knows best. And know that patience, in relation to faith, is in the position of the head in relation to the body; when the head is cut off, the body is gone; and there is no faith for one who has no patience.”

records.text_ar: 74 - قَالَ الزُّبَيْرُ: وَكَانَ عَلِيٌّ عليه السلام ، يَقُولُ: ‌ ‌«لَطَلَبُ الْمَالِ وَالْمُرُوءَةِ أَسْرَعُ فِي خَرَابِ دِينِ الرَّجُلِ مِنْ ذِئْبَيْنِ ضَارِيَيْنِ بَاتَا فِي حَظِيرَةِ غَنَمٍ ، فَمَاذَا أَبْقَيَا حِينَ أَصْبَحَا؟»
records.text_en: 74 – Al-Zubayr said: ʿAlī ﵇ used to say: “The pursuit of wealth and reputation (murūʾa) hastens the ruin of a man’s religion more than two ravening wolves that spend the night in a sheepfold: what do they leave when morning comes?”

records.text_ar: 75 - وَبِهِ عَنِ الْحَارِثِ ، قَالَ: أَتَيْتُ عَلِيًّا عليه السلام ، فَقُلْتُ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ،‌ ‌ مَا الإِيمَانُ؟ فَسِّرْهُ لِي ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ: " يَا حَارِثُ إِنَّ الإِيمَانَ شَيْءٌ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ دَعَائِمَ: عَلَى الصَّبْرِ ، وَالْيَقِينِ ، وَالْعَدْلِ ، وَالْجِهَادِ ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: فَعَلامَ بُنِيَ الصَّبْرُ؟ قَالَ: بُنِيَ الصَّبْرُ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ شُعَبٍ: عَلَى الشَّوْقِ ، وَالشَّفَقِ ، وَالزُّهْدِ ، وَالتَّرَقُّبِ ، فَمَنِ اشْتَاقَ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ سَلا عَنِ الشَّهَوَاتِ ، وَمَنْ أَشْفَقَ مِنَ النَّارِ رَجَعَ عَنِ الْحُرُمَاتِ ، وَمَنْ زَهِدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا تَهَاوَنَ بِالْمُصِيبَاتِ ، وَمَنْ رَاقَبَ الْمَوْتَ سَارَعَ إِلَى الْخَيْرَاتِ. قَالَ: قُلْتُ: فَعَلامَ بُنِيَ الْيَقِينُ؟ قَالَ: عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ شُعَبٍ: عَلَى تَبْصِرَةِ الْفِطْنَةِ ، وَتِلاوَةِ الْحِكْمَةِ ، وَمَوْعِظَةِ الْعِبْرَةِ ، وَسُنَّةِ الأَوَّلِينَ ، قَالَ: فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ الْفِطْنَةَ تَلا الْحِكْمَةَ ، وَمَنْ تَلا الْحِكْمَةَ عَرَفَ الْعِبْرَةَ ، وَمَنْ عَرَفَ الْعِبْرَةَ فَكَأَنَّمَا كَانَ فِي الأَوَّلِينَ ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: فَعَلامَ بُنِيَ الْعَدْلُ؟ قَالَ: بُنِيَ الْعَدْلُ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ شُعَبٍ: عَلَى غَايَةِ الْفَهْمِ ، وَرَوْضَةِ الْحِلْمِ ، وَزَهْرَةِ الْعِلْمِ ، وَشَرَائِعِ الْحِكْمَةِ ، فَمَنْ فَهِمَ فَسَّرَ الْعِلْمَ ، وَمَنْ فَسَّرَ الْعِلْمَ عَرَفَ شَرَائِعَ الْحِكْمَةِ ، وَمَنْ عَرَفَ شَرَائِعَ الْحِكْمَةِ حَلُمَ ، وَمَنْ حَلُمَ أَبْصَرَ أَمْرَهُ وَعَاشَ فِي الدُّنْيَا حَمِيدًا " قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ: فَعَلامَ بُنِيَ الْجِهَادُ؟ قَالَ: بَخٍ بَخٍ ، سَيِّدُ أَعْمَالِكُمْ وَأَسَاسُ دِينِكُمْ وَقَوَامُ أُمُورِكُمْ ، فَالْجِهَادُ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ شُعَبٍ: لَيْسَ عَلَى ضَرْبٍ بِالسَّيْفِ وَحْدَهُ ، وَلَكِنْ أَمْرٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ ، وَنَهْيٌ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ ، وَالصَّبْرُ فِي الْمَوَاطِنِ ، وَشَنَآنُ الْفَاسِقِينَ. قَالَ: فَمَنْ أَمَرَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ شَدَّ ظَهْرَ الْمُؤْمِنِ ، وَمَنْ نَهَى عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ رَغِمَ أَنْفُ الْمُنَافِقِ ، وَمَنْ صَبَرَ فِي الْمَوَاطِنِ قَضَى الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ ، وَمَنْ غَضِبَ لِلَّهِ وَشَنَأَ الْفَاسِقِينَ غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عز وجل لَهُ "
records.text_en: 75 – And by it, from al-Ḥārith, who said: I came to ʿAlī ﵇ and said: O Commander of the Believers, what is faith? Explain it to me. He said: “O Ḥārith, faith is a thing on four pillars: on patience, certainty, justice, and jihād. He said: I said: On what is patience built? He said: Patience is built on four branches: on longing (shawq), apprehension (shafaq), asceticism (zuhd), and anticipation (tarqqub); so whoever longs for Paradise turns away from base desires, and whoever is apprehensive of the Fire turns back from the forbidden things, and whoever is ascetic in this world treats afflictions lightly, and whoever keeps watch for death hastens to good deeds. He said: I said: On what is certainty built? He said: On four branches: on the insight of sagacity, the recitation of wisdom, the admonition of lessons, and the practice (sunna) of the ancients. He said: Whoever has insight into sagacity recites wisdom, and whoever recites wisdom knows the lesson, and whoever knows the lesson is as though he were among the ancients. He said: I said: On what is justice built? He said: Justice is built on four branches: on the utmost of understanding, the garden of forbearance, the flower of knowledge, and the paths (sharāʾiʿ) of wisdom; so whoever understands explains knowledge, and whoever explains knowledge knows the paths of wisdom, and whoever knows the paths of wisdom is forbearing, and whoever is forbearing sees his affair clearly and lives in this world praised.” He said: I said: On what is jihād built? He said: “Excellent, excellent! It is the master of your deeds, the foundation of your religion, and the support of your affairs. Jihād is on four branches: not merely striking with the sword, but commanding the right (maʿrūf), forbidding the wrong (munkar), patience in the battle stations, and detestation of the transgressors. He said: Whoever commands the right strengthens the back of the believer; whoever forbids the wrong has the hypocrite’s nose rubbed in the dust; whoever is patient in the stations has fulfilled what is upon him; and whoever becomes angry for God and detests the transgressors, God, Mighty and Majestic, becomes angry for him.”

records.text_ar: 76 - وَبِهِ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي الزُّبَيْرُ ، عَنِ الْمَعْرُورِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ ، قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ‌ ‌ يَتَوَضَّأُ لِلصَّلاةِ مَرَّتَيْنِ مَرَّتَيْنِ . وَبِهِ نا الْحَجَّاجُ ، نا بِشْرٌ ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ أَبِي النُّجُودِ ، عَنِ الْمَعْرُورِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ ، عَنْ عُمَرَ ، مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ
records.text_en: 76 – And by it he said: Al-Zubayr narrated to me, from al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd, who said: I saw ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb perform ablution for the prayer twice each. And by it al-Ḥajjāj informed us: Bishr informed us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī l-Najūd, from al-Maʿrūr ibn Suwayd, from ʿUmar, the like of that.

records.text_ar: 77 - وَبِهِ نا بِشْرٌ ، عَنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنِي، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبَّاسٍ دَخَلَ عَلَى عُمَرَ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ ، فَقَالَ: " أَبْشِرْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ،‌ ‌ أَبْشِرْ بِالْجَنَّةِ ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: مَهْ. قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: بَلَى ، أَسْلَمْتَ حِينَ كَفَرُوا ، وَجَاهَدْتَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حِينَ خَذَلُوهُ ، وَتُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ عَنْكَ رَاضٍ " نا بِشْرٌ ، قَالَ: تَلا الزُّبَيْرُ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ: {وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَذَا الْقُرْءَانُ لأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَنْ بَلَغَ} [الأنعام: 19] . مَنْ بَلَغَهُ الْقُرْآنُ ، فَكَأَنَّمَا هُوَ قَدْ عَايَنَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَالنَّبِيِّينَ قَبْلَهُ ، ثُمَّ تَلا: {وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَذَا الْقُرْءَانُ لأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَنْ بَلَغَ} [الأنعام: 19] حَدَّثَنِي الزُّبَيْرُ ، قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ النَّخَعِيِّ، قَالَ: أَرَأَيْتَ الْإِمَامَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ أَيَخْطُبُ جَالِسًا أَوْ قَائِمًا؟ فَقَالَ لَهُ: كَيْفَ تَقْرَأُ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: {وَإِذَا رَأَوْا تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْوًا انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ} [الجمعة: 11] . قَائِمًا أَوْ قَاعِدًا؟ قَالَ: بَلْ أَقْرَؤُهَا: {قَائِمًا} [الجمعة: 11] . قَالَ: فَهُوَ ذَلِكَ. عَنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ النَّخَعِيِّ ، فَقَالَ: إِنَّ أُمِّي إِذَا أَرَادَتِ الْوُضُوءَ أَخَذَتِ الْمَاءَ بِيَدِهَا ، ثُمَّ صَبَّتْهُ ، ثُمَّ مَسَحَتْ وَجْهَهَا بِكَفَّيْهَا ، قَالَ: فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ النَّخَعِيُّ ، ثُمّ أَعَادَ عَلَيْهِ الثَّانِيَةِ ، فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ ، ثُمَّ أَعَادَ الثَّالِثَةَ ، فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ، ثُمَّ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ: وَهَلِ الْوُضُوءُ إِلا هَكَذَا؟ مَا عَهِدْنَاهُمْ يَلْطِمُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ بِالْمَاءِ.
records.text_en: 77 – And by it Bishr informed us, from al-Zubayr, who said: It reached me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās entered upon ʿUmar at his death and said: “Rejoice, O Commander of the Believers; rejoice in Paradise. ʿUmar said: Enough! Ibn ʿAbbās said: Indeed: you accepted Islam when they disbelieved, and you waged jihād alongside the Messenger of God ﷺ when they abandoned him, and the Messenger of God ﷺ died while he was pleased with you.” Bishr informed us, saying: al-Zubayr recited this verse: {And this Qurʾān was revealed to me that I may warn you by it and whomever it reaches} [al-Anʿām: 19]. Whomever the Qurʾān reaches, it is as though he had seen the Messenger of God ﷺ and the prophets before him; then he recited: {And this Qurʾān was revealed to me that I may warn you by it and whomever it reaches} [al-Anʿām: 19]. Al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: A man came to Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and said: What is your opinion: does the imam on the day of Friday give the sermon sitting or standing? He said to him: How do you read in the Book of God: {And when they see trade or amusement, they scatter to it and leave you} [al-Jumuʿa: 11] — standing or sitting? He said: I read it: {standing} [al-Jumuʿa: 11]. He said: Then that is it. From al-Zubayr, who said: A man came to Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and said: When my mother wants to perform ablution, she takes the water in her hand, then pours it out, then wipes her face with her palms. He said: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī turned away from him; then he repeated it to him a second time, and he turned away from him; then he repeated it a third time, and Ibrāhīm turned away from him; then Ibrāhīm said: Is ablution anything but this? We never knew them to slap their faces with water.

records.text_ar: 78 - حَدَّثَنِي الزُّبَيْرُ ، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ ، قَالَ: جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ إِلَى ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، فَقَالَ: " إِنِّي رَاعٍ إِبِلَ أَهْلِي ، فَأَعْزُبُ عَنْهُمُ اللَّيْلَتَيْنِ وَالثَّلاثَ ، فَيَمُرُّ بِي الْمَارُّ فَيَسْتَسْقِي ، أَفَأَسْقِيهِ؟ قَالَ: لا. قَالَ: قَدْ ذَهَبَ الأَعْرَابِيُّ ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: رُدَّهُ ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: كَيْفَ قُلْتَ؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ:‌ ‌ إِنِّي رَاعٍ إِبِلَ أَهْلِي فَأَعْزُبُ عَنْهُمُ اللَّيْلَتَيْنِ وَالثَّلاثَ ، فَيَمُرُّ بِي الْمَارُّ فَيَسْتَسْقِي ، أَفَأَسْقِيهِ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ ، قَدْرَ مَا يُبَلِّغُهُ إِلَيَّ غَيْرُكَ ، ثُمَّ اسْتَأْذِنْ مَوَالِيكَ "
records.text_en: 78 – Al-Zubayr narrated to me, from Masrūq, who said: A Bedouin came to Ibn ʿAbbās and said: “I herd my family’s camels, and I am away from them for two nights or three; and a passer-by passes me and asks for water; shall I give him to drink? He said: No. He said: The Bedouin went off; so Ibn ʿAbbās said: Bring him back. He said to him: What did you say? He said: I said: I herd my family’s camels and I am away from them for two nights or three, and a passer-by passes me and asks for water; shall I give him to drink? He said: Yes, as much as will carry him on to someone other than you; then ask permission of your masters.”

records.text_ar: 79 - حَدَّثَنِي الزُّبَيْرُ ، قَالَ: كَانَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ يَقُولُ: ‌ ‌«دِيَةُ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَالنَّصْرَانِيِّ أَرْبَعَةُ آلافٍ ، وَالْمَجُوسِيِّ ثَمَانُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ»
records.text_en: 79 – Al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to say: “The blood-money (diya) of the Jew and the Christian is four thousand, and of the Zoroastrian eight hundred dirhams.”
